audit.why: Level 1 even, level 2 his on an E pull into an isolated Obliterate, then Cassiopeia owns 3 through 5, Mordekaiser takes 6 on Realm of Death, and she reclaims it by two items. That shape matches the 59.32% over 118 games and both layers agree on the rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Realm of Death is called matchup-defining in four fields and 'the whole green-light system' with no cooldown given, and Indestructible was never given one either.
audit.why: Realm of Death is 140/120/100s at 650 range and Indestructible is 12/11/10/9/8s. A 140-second ultimate means most of the lane is played with his kill threat unavailable, which is the actual spike map here.
audit.corrected: 140s added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, whys[4] and mid; 12s added for Indestructible.

audit.whatIsWrong: FABRICATED ABILITY NAME: five fields call his W the 'Indignation shield' (spikes[0], spikes[3], early, late, wants.you[0]). His W is Indestructible. Separately, three fields tell the reader to 'ground his approach' with Miasma; Mordekaiser has no movement ability, so the grounding is a non-interaction. And nothing anywhere said that chipping him FEEDS the shield.
audit.why: Riot's kit: W Indestructible stores damage he deals and takes to create a shield, which he may consume to heal. Nothing in the kit is a dash, leap or blink, so Miasma's grounding has nothing to disable and only the slow does work. Because the shield banks damage he takes, sustained low-level poke into an active Indestructible is literally building his shield and heal - the correct pattern is burst it down, not chip at it. The missing-interactions file flags this matchup needs-antiheal for exactly that heal.
audit.corrected: All five 'Indignation' references replaced with Indestructible; the grounding claim replaced with the slow in wants.you[1], mid, late and dontsFull[1].d; the feed-the-shield rule stated in spikes[3].text, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit file tags Obliterate (Q) with a 'grounding' flag.
audit.why: Riot's own description is 'smashes the ground with his mace dealing damage to each enemy struck, damage increased when hitting a single enemy' - no grounding at all. The parser has read the word 'ground' out of the flavour text. Per the brief, the description wins. The same description gives a free concrete tip that was missing: Obliterate hits harder on an isolated target, so standing beside a minion cuts it.
audit.corrected: No text claims Mordekaiser grounds Cassiopeia. whys[1] now names the isolated Obliterate explicitly.

edits.before: Level 1 is even — he has one ability and so do you, no poison stacking yet, so just last-hit at the edge of Q range and stay outside his E (Death's Grasp) pull. Level 2 tips to him: with only Q and E at one rank each, your poison hasn't ramped, so if he lands E and an isolated Q (Obliterate) he can shield through your single Twin Fang and win that burst. Once you hit level 3 the lane flips — a full Q-into-E chain plus your move-speed kiting lets you prime him and spam refunded Twin Fangs faster than his Indignation shield re-forms. The whole early game is about not eating a blind E pull: bait it, sidestep, and never trade while his shield is fresh.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — he has one ability and so do you, no poison stacking yet, so just last-hit at the edge of Q range and stay outside his E (Death's Grasp) pull. Level 2 tips to him: with only Q and E at one rank each, your poison hasn't ramped, so if he lands E and an isolated Q (Obliterate) he can shield through your single Twin Fang and win that burst. Stand next to a minion and Obliterate hits for less. Once you hit level 3 the lane flips — a full Q-into-E chain plus your move-speed kiting lets you prime him and spam refunded Twin Fang faster than Indestructible re-forms. The early game is about not eating a blind E pull: bait it, sidestep, and never trade into a fresh shield.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are yours — extra ranks in Q and E let you chain near-continuous Twin Fangs, and with no dash he can't close the gap your boots-free Serpentine-Grace speed opens, so you kite and shred him in any drawn-out fight. Level 6 is his single biggest threat: Realm of Death rips you into a private 1v1, steals a portion of your AP and resistances, and inside that box a juggernaut beats a squishy caster — hold R (Petrifying Gaze) and Flash for it, hug your tower, and don't get caught alone when his ult is up. Lay W (Miasma) on his path to slow and ground his approach, then re-engage your poke once his shield drops.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours — extra ranks in Q and E let you chain near-continuous Twin Fang, and with no dash he can't close the gap your boots-free Serpentine-Grace speed opens, so you kite and shred him in any drawn-out fight. Level 6 is his single biggest threat: Realm of Death (140s at rank 1) rips you into a private 1v1, steals a portion of your AP and resistances, and inside that box a juggernaut beats a squishy caster — hold Flash for it, hug your tower, and don't get caught alone while it is up. Lay W (Miasma) on his path: he has no dash to ground, but the slow holds his melee frame out of Obliterate range.

edits.before: By first item you're a dominant lane DPS — Malignance or early Liandry's plus your passive AP-from-move-speed lets you poke him off the wave and kite his immobile frame all day. At 2+ items you become a single-target shredder: poisoned Twin Fangs chew through his Indignation shield faster than it can re-form, and with no real answer to your ramping DPS you out-duel the juggernaut outright. His only path back is a clean E pull or a perfect Realm of Death while you're isolated — so keep W ready to ground and slow his engage, never face him alone when R is up, and hold at the edge of your poison range where his melee kit can't reach.

notes: 'Indignation shield' is a fabricated ability name in five separate fields — his W is Indestructible — and it is the same class of error as the Brand and Cassiopeia cases in the calibration list. Second systemic issue: three fields told the player to ground Mordekaiser, who has no movement ability at all; the Miasma grounding line appears to be emitted generically for every Cassiopeia matchup (the already-audited Mel side traced this to a hardcoded row in champ-data/_gen-engine.js). Not verified and left alone: whether Realm of Death can be stopped by QSS or Cleanse, and whether Cassiopeia's Petrifying Gaze is castable during the drag animation — neither is in Riot's text.
